za-prinsevlag.title: Flag of South Africa (1928–1994)

colors.note: The Prince's Flag (Prinsenvlag) of the Netherlands.

desc:
- The Prinsevlag (Prince's Flag) of South Africa was an orange, white, and blue horizontal tricolour — derived from the Dutch Prince's Flag — flown as part of the apartheid-era national flag (1928–1994)
- The South African flag of 1928 incorporated a central panel showing the Prinsevlag alongside the Union Jack and the flags of the two Boer republics
- The Prinsevlag itself represented the Afrikaner heritage
- **Construction:** three horizontal stripes of orange (top), white, and blue. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The Prinsevlag (Prince's Flag) is an alternative South African flag design
- Represents historical Dutch/Afrikaner heritage
- Used by some cultural and historical societies
